rendered:
1. Aging (activation) of the bare NiTi superelastic wire, before any coating, at 600 °C for 1 h under vacuum[1] in a quartz CVD tube furnace. The aged wires were then mechanically polished and cleaned.
2. Atomic layer deposition of the vanadium oxide coating, run with a reaction temperature of 200 °C[2] maintained throughout the process. This is the deposition temperature, not a post-deposition treatment. The as-deposited coatings were poorly crystalline.
3. Post-deposition annealing of the coating, annealed at 450 °C for 30 min[3] in a Lindberg Blue quartz CVD tube furnace open to air, which gave crystalline V2O5 coatings on the wire.
